method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis' (last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at the RCH website Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the Wave 1 hand-written page (edition 1.0, 2026-09-22), which quoted RCH verbatim, as a paraphrase of the page re-fetched 2026-09-24. All 45 Wave 1 claims are carried over; the dose claims are now flagged as doses.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Orbital or intracranial spread from infective rhinosinusitis is uncommon**, but it is the complication to look for.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Allergic rhinitis:** reduce allergen exposure, give antihistamines, and add a nasal steroid where needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Neonatal rhinitis is common** and usually settles untreated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Rhinitis** is inflammation of the nasal lining and **rhinosinusitis** of the paranasal sinuses; the two often occur together. Rhinitis is either allergic (seasonal or perennial) or non-allergic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Rhinosinusitis by duration:** acute: under 4 weeks, usually infective · recurrent acute: 3 or more episodes in 6 months with symptom-free gaps of 10 days or longer, or 4 or more per 12 months · subacute: 4 to 12 weeks · chronic: beyond 12 weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Acute rhinosinusitis is mostly viral.** A secondary bacterial infection can follow, especially when symptoms last beyond 10 days.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Organisms:** viral — rhinovirus, RSV, influenza, adenovirus, often with wider viral symptoms; bacterial — *Streptococcus pneumoniae*, non-typeable *Haemophilus influenzae*, *Moraxella catarrhalis*.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Allergic rhinitis matters for asthma:** it raises the chance of developing asthma, worsens control, and shapes how asthma progresses into adult life.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The 'pig nose' manoeuvre:** tip the head back, lift the nasal tip with a thumb and shine a light or otoscope in. Look at the mucosa, the colour and size of the turbinates, and where the septum sits.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Reading the mucosa:** pale, boggy inferior turbinates fit allergic rhinitis; red, swollen mucosa points more to infection or a medication cause.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Allergic facies:** Dennie-Morgan lines, the allergic salute, allergic shiners, a transverse crease across the nose, mouth breathing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **History:** often a viral illness first · nasal discharge lasting over 10 days (whether it is purulent matters little) · pain in the maxillary teeth · facial pain on one side.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Acute otitis media is often found as well**, because the two share a cause.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Complications:** meningitis or encephalitis · cerebral abscess · subdural or epidural empyema · cavernous sinus thrombosis · periorbital and orbital cellulitis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Wait 3 days first:** a viral sinusitis looks the same and is the likelier cause, so allow time for it to settle. Start antibiotics if there is no improvement by then, or sooner if the child gets worse.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Antibiotics:** first line oral amoxicillin 15 mg/kg, up to 500 mg, three times daily × 5 days (cefalexin if penicillin-allergic). Not improving: switch to oral amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 22.5 mg/kg, up to 875 mg, every 12 hours × a further 5 days. Systemically unwell or cannot take oral: IV amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 25 mg/kg, up to 1 g, every 6 hours (ceftriaxone plus metronidazole if penicillin-allergic).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not take nasal swabs:** a nasal culture does not reflect the sinus organisms, so it does not help.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No benefit in acute sinusitis** from steroid sprays, decongestants or antihistamines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Surgery is very seldom needed** for acute bacterial sinusitis unless there is an orbital or intracranial complication.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **CT is the preferred imaging**, and is considered when medical treatment has failed, an orbital or intracranial complication is possible, or surgery is being weighed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Uncommon under 12 years.** Defined by 12 weeks or more of symptoms: nasal obstruction or congestion, discharge, facial pain, postnasal drip, cough, reduced smell, halitosis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Risk factors:** cigarette smoke exposure · adenoid hypertrophy · allergy · asthma · reflux · cystic fibrosis · physical obstruction · impaired mucociliary clearance · immune deficiency · long-term intranasal decongestant use.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Treat for at least 6 weeks:** saline spray or irrigation (sodium chloride, 2 sprays or irrigations each nostril twice daily and when needed, before the steroid) plus an intranasal corticosteroid, eg mometasone 50 microg spray — 2-12 y: 1 spray per nostril once a day · 12-18 y: 2 sprays per nostril once a day, stepping down to 1 per side when controlled.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Decongestants, oral or intranasal, have no place.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **If symptoms persist:** check adherence and spray technique, then refer to ENT if still not relieved.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Principles:** always alongside minimising common allergens (house dust mite, pollens, pet dander, mould) · give each step about 4 weeks before judging it · check adherence and spray technique before stepping up · use the least treatment that works.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Step 1 (mild):** one antihistamine, oral or intranasal; combining them adds nothing. Use it when needed for intermittent symptoms, or regularly for persistent ones.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Oral vs intranasal antihistamine:** oral works better on itch away from the nose, suits younger children better, and a less sedating agent is preferred; intranasal works better on nasal symptoms, acts faster, and needs good technique.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Cetirizine, for example:** 1-2 y: 2.5 mg as oral drops (5 drops) twice a day · 2-6 y: 5 mg once a day, or 2.5 mg twice a day · 6-12 y: 10 mg once a day, or 5 mg twice a day · 12-18 y: 10 mg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Azelastine nasal spray (1 mg/mL), for example:** over 5 years, 1 spray each nostril twice daily.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Step 2 (moderate-severe): add an intranasal corticosteroid.** Particularly good for blockage and also eases eye symptoms. Relief often begins within days, but judge it only after at least 4 weeks of steady use. Eg mometasone 50 microg spray — 2-12 y: 1 spray per nostril once a day · 12-18 y: 2 sprays per nostril once a day, then 1 per side when controlled.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Step 3:** where nasal symptoms dominate, consider switching to a combined antihistamine-corticosteroid nasal spray and stop any oral antihistamine. For example a fluticasone propionate + azelastine spray (125/50 microg), 6-18 y: 1 spray per nostril twice a day.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Step 4 (site-specific):** eye symptoms — ketotifen 0.025% drops, 3-18 years, 1 drop twice daily; for prevention of recurrent eye flares, olopatadine 0.1% drops, 3-18 years, 1 drop twice daily for up to 14 weeks. Intermittent allergic rhinitis with asthma: consider montelukast.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Allergen immunotherapy:** for moderate-severe symptoms that fail treatment including allergen minimisation; refer to immunology/allergy; subcutaneous (SCIT) or sublingual (SLIT) for 3 years or more. **It is not PBS-subsidised and the yearly cost can be substantial.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Newborns: no nasal antihistamines, decongestants, steroids or humidifiers.** Saline drops before feeds are fine; seek specialist review if breathing or feeding is affected.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Other causes to consider:** a foreign body (one-sided symptoms, brown discharge, sometimes visible, often a foul smell from that nostril) · hormonal (pregnancy or the menstrual cycle; in older children, subclinical hypothyroidism) · drugs, typically aspirin and other NSAIDs · rebound congestion, where overuse of topical decongestants inflames the nasal lining.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Idiopathic (vasomotor) rhinitis:** watery discharge that switches on and off abruptly, set off by strong smells or temperature changes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Recurrent or severe? Think of rarer causes:** cystic fibrosis, ciliary dysfunction, immunodeficiency, anatomical anomalies.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Diagnosis is usually clinical, with no tests.** In allergic rhinitis, testing does not make the diagnosis and must be read against the history: a positive result shows sensitisation only. It can guide allergen minimisation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Serum specific IgE vs skin prick:** serum specific IgE to environmental allergens (formerly RAST) is unaffected by anti-allergy medicines; skin prick testing is affected by them.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Paediatric team** for any systemically unwell child or suspected orbital/intracranial complication. **ENT** for suppurative complications or possible surgery, and for nasal obstruction that medical treatment has not fixed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Immunology/allergy referral:** more allergy testing and interpretation to guide allergen minimisation · severe or poorly controlled allergic rhinitis despite treatment · assessment for immunotherapy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transfer** if intracranial involvement is suspected, with altered consciousness, seizures or focal neurological signs.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Many brands exist**, and their price and access (over the counter or on prescription) vary.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Rhinitis and rhinosinusitis', last updated October 2025, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Rhinitis_and_rhinosinusitis/, retrieved 2026-09-24
